Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle surge & VAT on INV-OPS-202512

Hi Hannah / Ben,

We noticed a ~3.8x spike on our Dec 1–6 usage line on invoice INV-OPS-202512 (attached). The surge aligns with a scheduled batch embedding run we kicked off on Dec 1, but the magnitude looks higher than expected and VAT was applied differently across two line items (hosted vs dedicated).

Can you please:  
- Confirm whether those requests were attributed to our production key or a staging key that should have been excluded;
- Share a short usage slice (request IDs + timestamps + model + token counts) for Dec 1–6 so we can map to our job;
- Temporarily hold collection on the disputed amount while we reconcile — PO is on file but we need the trace to justify an adjustment.

We attached the invoice (INV-OPS-202512.pdf). If you need more, I can pull the job IDs from our side — let me know the format you prefer.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle surge & VAT on INV-OPS-202512 — initial findings

Hi all — quick engineering triage summary after pulling a sampled export for Dec 1–6 (attached: opsly-log-sample-20251207.csv):

Root cause hypothesis: a staging API key tied to Opsly’s account namespace was not excluded from production billing after a recent onboarding change. That key was used by an internal pipeline to run a batched streaming job; because streaming token accounting and batch requests were both being counted and our legacy prefetch dedupe rule didn’t trigger for that specific multipart payload, some tokens were double-attributed.

What I pulled: a 24-hour slice where we see two request_ids per logical operation (req_abc123 and req_abc123-part2) with identical payloads but different api_key_id values. One api_key_id maps to Opsly-prod, the other to Opsly-staging. Combined token accounting (tokens_in + tokens_out + streaming_frames) yields the inflated totals.

Provisional correction steps:  
- Generate a corrected token count by collapsing multipart siblings (dedupe on original_request_id header) and attributing all to the production api_key;
- Provide a CSV export with raw rows + corrected_token_count and a delta column you can use to reconcile against your job. Sample available in the attached.
- Proposed provisional credit = sum(delta_tokens * rate_per_token) across the deduped rows; we’ll show both gross and VAT components.

I recommend a temporary credit hold of the disputed line until we complete the full export and reconciliation. Estimated timeline: 24–48 hours to produce the full Dec 1–6 export and a provisional credit memo.

Attachment: opsly-log-sample-20251207.csv (text/csv)

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Billing Escalations | Redwood Inference

- Please share the full Dec 1–6 export and the deduped CSV. If possible, add a column showing the job_id or original_request_id so we can map to our internal records.
- Procurement is requesting an ETA for the credit memo and a confirmation that collection remains paused. We’ve attached our PO for reference (opsly-po-2025Q4.pdf).
